title: Conductor Panel: Capacity Playback & Throughput Inspector
creator: Claire Zhang
description:
Problem: Customers managing Dedicated fleets need a single place to understand historical scaling decisions, inspect the effective throughput guarantees over time, and perform safe rollbacks. Current Console views are fragmented: separate scaling controls, throughput charts, and audit logs without a coherent, actionable surface.

Proposal: Build a 'Conductor Panel' — a compact, operator-facing UI that brings together
  - an interactive throughput ledger (hourly and per-route throughput guarantees),
  - a capacity playback slider to replay scaling events and visualize effective concurrency and queue length,
  - compact autoscale policy editor (rate windows + burst caps) with immediate validation, and
  - an immutable change inspector with side-by-side before/after snapshots + one-click rollback to a prior policy version.

Scope (MVP): playback + throughput ledger + readonly change inspector + manual rollback. Integration with autoscale automation and predictive suggestions deferred to follow-up. Focus on high signal: show per-fleet and per-route lines, annotate policy changes, annotate incidents and customer tickets that correlate with scaling events.
acceptance_criteria: Conductor Panel is discoverable from Fleet > Actions > Conductor Panel
Playback slider can replay last 72 hours of capacity events with at least 1-minute granularity
Throughput ledger displays per-route committed throughput and observed TPS on the same time scale
Change inspector lists all policy changes with author, timestamp, diff summary, and links to the full policy JSON
Manual rollback to a prior policy version is gated by an approval modal that requires a short rationale and records the operator
All actions are recorded in the existing audit log and surface a GitHub-style event id for traceability
Performance: initial panel load completes in under 700ms for fleets up to 50 nodes; playback rendering remains <200ms per step

2026-03-04 Design review (DES-3290): inline diffs and small-microcopy for rollback confirmation requested. Designer suggests color treatment for committed vs observed throughput lines to aid colorblind users.

2026-03-05 PM note: Prioritize immutable change ids + linkable snapshots for audit/compliance. Legal asked for retention of 1 year of snapshots — added to scope as non-blocking for MVP UI but must be backfilled for release.

2026-03-07 ENG feedback: playback rendering should use sampling at high event rates to keep CPU low; proposed approach: aggregate to 1s buckets above 100 events/s. Marked as tech decision in ENG-78421.
2026-03-08 Security review: rollback action must include CSRF protection + operator 2FA check if customer_impact=high. Security to provide checklist by 2026-03-12.
2026-03-09 QA: Created test plan with synthetic load scenarios and recorded golden outputs. Filing QA bugs after initial demo. QA ticket: ENG-80211.

2026-03-10 Claire Z.: Demoed prototype to 2 pilot customers (fintech & e-commerce). Both liked playback and rollback; asked for a CSV export of throughput ledger and ability to pin a snapshot to incidents. Adding to backlog.
Next steps: finalize API schema with ENG, implement mock data in Console staging, run design accessibility pass, and schedule security sign-off.
